nodes.label: CookTorrance.frag (main lighting fragment shader)
nodes.rationale: The renderer's main surface shader: samples albedo, sums the rendering equation over every light with shadowing, blends in hemispheric ambient and writes raw HDR radiance.

nodes.label: Cook-Torrance microfacet BRDF
nodes.rationale: The surface is treated statistically as a crowd of microscopic mirrors; fr = clamp(N.L) * (k*mD + (1-k)*mS*D*F*G / (4*(N.L)*(N.V))), the form E06 slides 38-39 give. It replaced an ad-hoc Blinn specular chosen because it looked right.

nodes.label: D: GGX normal distribution
nodes.rationale: The fraction of microfacets oriented along the half vector h, and therefore the highlight itself; roughness enters here and widens the lobe. GGX was chosen over Blinn for its long tail: a narrow core fading into a wide halo, as real surfaces behave.

nodes.label: G: geometric self-shadowing term
nodes.rationale: Parameter-free min-form (E06 s.47) accounting for microfacets shadowing and masking each other; without it rough surfaces blow out absurdly bright at grazing angles.

nodes.label: F: Schlick Fresnel approximation
nodes.rationale: The fraction reflected rather than transmitted, rising from F0 head-on to 1 at the horizon; the exponent 5 is Schlick's fit, not a derivation. It is the term that makes every matte surface mirror-like at grazing view, which Blinn has no counterpart for.

nodes.label: 4*(N.L)*(N.V) microfacet-area normalization
nodes.rationale: Converts from the area of the microfacets to the area of the surface carrying them; explicitly flagged in the comments as the one part of the formula that looks arbitrary and is not.

nodes.label: max(..., 0.0001) silhouette NaN guard
nodes.rationale: The specular denominator hits zero exactly at the silhouette; NdotL zeroes the result there anyway, but inf * 0 is a NaN and a NaN spreads through everything it touches, so the denominator is floored.

nodes.label: Lambert diffuse half
nodes.rationale: E06 s.38 prescribes Lambert as Cook-Torrance's diffuse component; Oren-Nayar was deliberately not folded in because swapping the diffuse model would stop it being the model the slides describe.

nodes.label: Clamped N.L (no negative light)
nodes.rationale: A face turned away from a light contributes zero instead of a negative amount; without this a lantern behind a wall would subtract light another source put there, and the symptom would be objects darkening as a light approaches.

nodes.label: k: diffuse/specular interpolation, not addition
nodes.rationale: The two halves are interpolated by k rather than summed, because adding both at full strength lets a surface return more light than it received; it is also why metals read right, since a metal has k near zero.

nodes.label: Per-model material parameters (mS, roughness, F0, k)
nodes.rationale: The Cook-Torrance authoring set replacing mS + specular exponent; mS stays because the professor's formulation keeps specular colour and Fresnel base reflectance separate, unlike modern PBR's RGB F0. F0 is ~0.04 for every dielectric and roughness has a physical 0..1 meaning, so both are easier to author than an exponent with no scale.

nodes.label: Rendering equation as a light loop
nodes.rationale: The inner loop is literally the scanline form of the rendering equation: a sum over sources of radiance times BRDF, each term multiplied by that light's shadow factor. Its legitimacy rests on every term being non-negative.

nodes.label: Three light types behind two functions
nodes.rationale: Direct, point and spot differ only in lightDirection() and lightRadiance(); the BRDF never learns which kind it was handed. A spot is not a new light model, it is a point light multiplied by a cone term (L09 s.31).

nodes.label: (g/dist)^beta distance decay
nodes.rationale: L09 s.22-23 decay with both g (the distance at which the light is exactly its colour) and beta authored per light; beta is deliberately not the physical 2, because with no real indirect lighting inverse-square reads as far too dark.

nodes.label: Spot cone falloff and its sign convention
nodes.rationale: Smooth clamp between cosOut and cosIn (angles authored as full degrees and converted to half-angle cosines once at load). The slides write the term against lx, the vector towards the light, while the data file stores the direction the lamp points, hence the explicit negation.

nodes.label: Hemispheric ambient (indirect light)
nodes.rationale: E07 s.47-54: mix(ambientLower, ambientUpper, (dot(N, ambientDir)+1)/2) times mD. A constant ambient claims light arrives equally from every direction, which outdoors is plainly false, so the term is made to depend on the normal; it is the smallest step that is genuinely a model rather than a fudge factor.

nodes.label: interiorAmbient: blend pinned at 0.5 indoors
nodes.rationale: Indoors neither end of the hemisphere model exists; taking the ground end literally made a dungeon ceiling collect ambientLower alone, 1.80x darker than the walls it meets and brown where they are cool. The flag pins the weight at the value a vertical surface gets.

nodes.label: Ambient as a share, not a sum
nodes.rationale: color = Lo*(1-aw) + ambient*aw, E17's blend. Summing instead made hemispheric ambient a brightness floor under every pixel: it has no visibility term, so a sealed room collected the same indirect light as the open courtyard and no ceiling could stop it.

nodes.label: ambientShare(): per-model ambient weight override
nodes.rationale: E17's single gubo.ambientLight knob made per-model, so a dungeon corridor and an open courtyard can hold different values in one frame. A negative material value means 'no override' and falls back to the scene default.

nodes.label: Authored enclosure is not ambient occlusion
nodes.rationale: The comment is explicit that the ambient share is a per-model authored guess at enclosure, not occlusion; the MGCG pack ships albedo only, so an AO map has nothing to read and baking one is named as the honest fix.

nodes.label: Shadows never darken the ambient term
nodes.rationale: shadowFactor only zeroes a light's direct contribution; leaving ambient untouched is what keeps a shadow reading as a dim indirectly-lit area instead of a hole into pure black.

nodes.label: 2D orthographic shadow map (the sun)
nodes.rationale: Direct and spot lights project the fragment into light space, remap XY to 0..1 and compare the stored closest depth. Only the sun uses it today; NUM_SHADOW_MAPS_2D is 2 to leave headroom for a future shadow-casting spot.

nodes.label: Cube shadow map (point lights)
nodes.rationale: A point light gets a real 6-face cube map instead of a 2D slot, because a single perspective map covers at most a hemisphere and a torch radiates in every direction. Sampled by direction, so it always has an answer and needs no covered/fallback dance.

nodes.label: Flat world-unit cube bias (0.03)
nodes.rationale: Because the cube stores a linear distance, one constant buys the same real-world slack in every direction, replacing the slope-scaled min/max pair a warped projective depth required.

nodes.label: Depth bias chosen per projection kind
nodes.rationale: A bias is an offset in the map's 0..1 depth, so how many centimetres it buys depends entirely on how the projection distributes depth; the sun's ortho box spreads 1..200 linearly so 0.0015 is a fixed ~30cm, while a perspective map crowds its range into the first metre.

nodes.label: Slope-scaled bias for perspective maps
nodes.rationale: mix(0.0004, 0.0030, 1-NdotL): head-on surfaces need almost none, edge-on ones need much more. Kept for a hypothetical shadow-casting spot now that the torches have moved to cube maps.

nodes.label: w <= 0 reject (points behind the light)
nodes.rationale: For a perspective matrix w is the view-space distance in front of the camera; without the check the perspective divide mirrors a point behind the light back into the map's 0..1 range and samples a depth belonging to a completely different direction.

nodes.label: Out-of-map UV/depth reject
nodes.rationale: Outside the sun's fixed ortho box there is nothing to compare against; missing the check would sample garbage at the map's clamped edge instead of returning fully lit.

nodes.label: One binding per shadow map instead of an array binding
nodes.rationale: Scene::init's descriptor-pool accounting counts bindings rather than the descriptors an array binding needs, so an array would silently under-reserve the pool; the cost is a hand-written if-chain in sampleShadowCube().

nodes.label: Set 2: per-shadow-casting-light descriptors
nodes.rationale: Shadow resources get their own set because their update frequency is neither once per frame (set 0) nor once per object (set 1) but once per shadow-casting light.

nodes.label: std140 vec3-then-float packing idiom
nodes.rationale: std140 gives a vec3 16-byte alignment and 12-byte size, so a following float fills the padding for free in GLSL and C++ alike; lightCount, debugFlags, time and ambientWeight all ride in padding so the light array still starts at a fixed offset.

nodes.label: Show Normals debug view
nodes.rationale: Writes N*0.5+0.5 as colour, placed after the flatNormals block so it shows the normal the lighting actually used, faceted faces included; it is the view that proved the MGCG meshes average their normals across hard edges.

nodes.label: Fullbright / unlit debug view
nodes.rationale: Albedo straight out with no lighting, which tells a black pixel that no light reached apart from a black pixel in the texture; the same bisect-the-shader trick that exposed the double gamma correction.

nodes.label: Specular off via k = 1
nodes.rationale: Not a branch in the BRDF: k is the diffuse share, so forcing it to 1 leaves the specular term multiplied by zero and everything else untouched, and BRDF keeps taking all its inputs as arguments.

nodes.label: Light-intensity heatmap view
nodes.rationale: Recolours by incoming light intensity ignoring albedo, through a log-compressed black-blue-green-yellow-red ramp because the input is unclamped HDR radiance and a linear ramp would read as solid red across a whole lit room.

nodes.label: Shadows-off cheat
nodes.rationale: Forces every shadowFactor() to 1, read directly from gubo.debugFlags rather than through debugOn() because that helper is declared further down the file.

nodes.label: Debug branches are uniform branches
nodes.rationale: Every debug flag is off in a normal frame and constant across a draw, so every pixel takes the same side of the branch, which is the cheap kind on a GPU.

nodes.label: Tone mapping moved out of the surface shader
nodes.rationale: The L09 s.45 HDR tone map c/(Y(c)+1) now runs once in Composite.frag: tone mapping compresses everything into [0,1] and the bloom bright pass works by finding pixels above 1, so compressing here would destroy the only thing it looks for.

nodes.label: Raw unclamped HDR output into an RGBA16F target
nodes.rationale: The main pass writes linear, unclamped radiance so a surface receiving more than a unit of light keeps saying so instead of being cut off at white; the bloom passes read that excess before the composite compresses it.

nodes.label: Per-pixel near-zero-radiance early out
nodes.rationale: Point/spot lights are only CPU-culled by distance to the camera, so a torch that passed that cull can still be negligible at a fragment across a large room; rejecting below 1e-3 skips the BRDF's pows and, more importantly, a dependent shadow-map fetch.

nodes.label: flatNormals: face normal from screen-space derivatives
nodes.rationale: dFdx/dFdy of the world position lie in the triangle's plane so their cross product is exactly perpendicular to it; the sign depends on winding, so it is oriented against the interpolated vertex normal, which is unreliable in magnitude but good at saying which side is out.

nodes.label: Renormalizing the interpolated normal
nodes.rationale: Linear interpolation shortens the vector wherever the three corner normals diverge, which is precisely where a smooth surface needs it correct; the vertex stage deliberately leaves it unnormalized since the fragment stage must do it anyway.

nodes.label: Hardware sRGB, no manual gamma in the shader
nodes.rationale: The albedo image view is R8G8B8A8_SRGB so the sampler already returns linear values; the skeleton's inherited pow(2.2)/pow(1/2.2) pair was a second decode and encode, collapsing dark and mid tones to black while white survived. The rule stated in notes.md is do the conversion once.
